kernelIdea: The complement of A in S is everything in S not in A — so it depends on S. Proof by contradiction: assume the negation of what you want, derive an impossibility, conclude.

kernels.l1: Everything not in the box depends on what room you are in.
kernels.l2: The outside of a box is everything else — but you have to say what everything else means first. And here is a new trick: to show something is true, suppose not, and watch it go wrong.
kernels.l3: The complement of A is everything in the surrounding set that is not in A, so it changes when the surrounding set changes. To prove something by contradiction, suppose not: assume the opposite, follow it until it says something impossible, and conclude the opposite was wrong.
kernels.l4: The complement of a set is everything in the surrounding universe that is not in it — so the universe must be named. Proof by contradiction: assume the opposite, derive an impossibility, and conclude the original.
kernels.l5: Complement is relative to a stated universe. A proof by contradiction assumes the negation of the goal and derives an impossibility, which is the natural method when the goal is itself a negation.
kernels.l6: A complement depends on the ambient set. *Suppose not* is licensed by the fact that one of a statement and its denial always holds, together with a contradiction refuting whatever was assumed.
kernels.l7: Complementation is defined relative to a surrounding set and is the set-level mirror of negation. Proof by contradiction assumes the denial, derives an impossibility, and concludes the original — reach for it when the goal is negative or says that nothing exists.
kernels.l8: Complement makes P(X) a Boolean algebra; reductio ad absurdum is classically valid but constructively suspect, and distinguishing it from proof of a negation is the constructive fault line.
